title: Allowance Rate Where the Promise Has Passed or Rework Was Found
content:
# Tariff Rider: The Allowance Rate Where the Promise Has Passed or Rework Was Found

This rider fixes the allowance rate carried on a work order of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service by reference to two records on that order: whether the promised date has passed at the handling date, and whether a check stands on the order that found rework needed.

| The promised date has passed | A check that found rework needed stands on the order | The allowance rate |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the wide contingency rate, 20 percent |
| yes | no | the standard contingency rate, 12 percent |
| no | yes | the standard contingency rate, 12 percent |
| no | no | the rate is not stepped up on these grounds |

**The rider in words.** Where the promised date has passed and a check stands on the work order that found rework needed, the allowance rate is the wide contingency rate of 20 percent; where exactly one of those two holds — the promised date has passed and no such check stands, or a check that found rework needed stands and the promised date has not passed — the allowance rate is the standard contingency rate of 12 percent. In any other case the rate is not stepped up on these grounds.

**On the two records.** The promised date is the day standing on the work order as the day the piece is promised back, and it has passed when the handling date is later than it; a promised date falling on the handling date itself has not passed. A check that found rework needed is one recorded against that work order whose finding was that rework was required, whenever it was logged.
